name: Resource Lease / Lock
purpose: A filesystem lease/lock so several processes on this one machine arbitrate contended resources: acquire/release/renew/status/list/check a named lease with a TTL. Atomic (CreateNew = open O_CREAT|O_EXCL), race-safe stale reclaim, holder identity + a lease_id token, blocking or non-blocking acquire. Conventional resources: gpu (one model run at a time), git (commit lock), doc:<path> (doc-ownership). v0.2 adds an ADDITIVE, DEFAULT-OFF fencing/handoff surface (a plain acquire is byte-identical to v0.1): a monotonic per-resource fencing token + CAS guard (finding 1), two lease kinds exec|residency_pin with fencing-backed priority revocation (finding 13), a prepared/evict-before-grant handoff over a pluggable evictor seam (findings 2/15), and lock-order-inversion rejection (finding 14). v0.3 (R1b) adds, still ADDITIVE + DEFAULT-OFF: THREE-IDENTITY fencing (gpu_authority_epoch = the per-resource fencing token, bumped only when exclusive GPU authority changes; resident_generation = the PoolManager-owned per-launch generation; exec_lease_id = the exec acquire's lease_id) with a full-tuple authority_ok assertion on check; the single scheduler-owned ATOMIC hand-off -Transition (reserve -> fence old owner -> drain/cancel -> evict OUTSIDE the lease mutex via a txn journal -> confirm tree gone -> confirm STABLE headroom across N observations -> grant, committing ONLY if the reserved authority epoch is still current); an ADVERSARIAL mock evictor; and crash reconcile of a PREPARING/DRAINING/STARTING transition. The multi-instance coordination primitive.

inputs.name: action
inputs.description: acquire | release | renew | status | list | check (one per invocation).

inputs.name: resource
inputs.description: The resource name (required for all but list). Conventional: gpu, git, doc:<path>; any string works.

inputs.name: holder
inputs.description: Stable identity of the caller. Default: $env:LIFEORCH_INSTANCE, else <host>:<pid>:<guid8>. Set a stable holder per instance so re-attach + release-by-holder work.

inputs.name: ttl_seconds
inputs.description: acquire/renew: the lease lifetime; an expired lease is reclaimable. Renew before it expires.

inputs.name: wait_seconds
inputs.description: acquire: block/poll up to this long for the resource to free. 0 = try once (non-blocking).

inputs.name: lease_id
inputs.description: release/renew: the token returned by acquire (proves you hold this exact lease).

inputs.name: note
inputs.description: Free text stored in the lease (e.g. what the holder is doing).

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: v0.2. exec (default = today's short execution/transition lease) | residency_pin (the REVOCABLE right to stay resident between exec ops). A pin is ALWAYS revocable; a higher-priority acquire revokes a lower-priority pin. Supplying -Kind (or any v0.2 input) engages the additive surface (returns fencing fields); omitting all of them is byte-identical to v0.1.

inputs.name: priority
inputs.description: v0.2. Higher wins. An acquire whose priority exceeds a resident revocable pin's priority REVOKES that pin (writes revoked_by + the new fencing_token into it) so the pinned holder learns on its next renew/check it has lost authority.

inputs.name: revocable
inputs.description: v0.2. A residency_pin is ALWAYS revocable; -Kind residency_pin with revocable=false is a hard STOP (error non_revocable_pin_forbidden).

inputs.name: fencing_token
inputs.description: v0.2. renew/release/check CAS guard: if supplied and it is not the resource's CURRENT token, the op is refused (reason/fence_status:fence_stale) -- a superseded holder is FENCED OUT.

inputs.name: required_vram_mib
inputs.description: v0.2 acquire. >=0 engages the PREPARED / evict-before-grant handoff (AcquirePreparedGpu-style): detect an incompatible/lower-priority resident pin, drive its revocation, and grant only AFTER the evictor seam confirms free headroom >= required_vram_mib + target_headroom_mib.

inputs.name: target_headroom_mib
inputs.description: v0.2 prepared. Extra free VRAM the evictor seam must confirm beyond required_vram_mib (the target-headroom invariant, finding 15).

inputs.name: evictor_mode
inputs.description: v0.2 prepared. none (no evictor -- grant only if the slot is already free) | mock (the built-in test evictor) | command (invoke -EvictorCommand as the pluggable seam -- the R1b PoolManager integration point). res.lease stays PURE: it never inspects VRAM or kills a server; the seam does.

inputs.name: mock_evictor_result
inputs.description: v0.2 prepared / v0.3 transition, mock evictor. v0.2: confirm | needs_evict | timeout. v0.3 adversarial additions (transition): late_evict (eviction completes late, then headroom stable -> grants: proves we WAIT for confirmation), partial_tree_term (headroom looks fine but the managed tree did NOT fully exit -> do NOT grant), headroom_never (target headroom never reached), headroom_fell (reached then fell -> not stable), cancel_during_prepare (a cancellation arrives mid-prepare -> abort, no grant).

inputs.name: mock_free_vram_mib
inputs.description: v0.2 prepared, mock evictor: the free VRAM it reports (0 = auto = just-enough to meet required+headroom).

inputs.name: evictor_command
inputs.description: v0.2 prepared, command mode: a pwsh script invoked as `& <script> -ContextJson <json>` that must emit a JSON {confirmed, free_vram_mib, evicted, outcome} result. The real PoolManager evictor (R1b) plugs in here.

inputs.name: confirm_interval_ms
inputs.description: v0.2 prepared. The WDDM-async headroom-confirmation interval passed to the evictor seam (VRAM frees asynchronously after an evict).

inputs.name: confirm_timeout_ms
inputs.description: v0.2 prepared. Give up confirming headroom after this (-> reason:headroom_timeout, no grant).

inputs.name: allow_lock_order
inputs.description: v0.2 acquire. Override the lock-order-inversion rejection (finding 14) with a recorded reason. Without it, acquiring a later/cheaper-ranked resource (git/doc:<path>) while THIS holder already holds an earlier-ranked one (gpu, then git) is rejected fail-closed (error lock_order_violation).

inputs.name: lock_order_reason
inputs.description: v0.2 acquire. The recorded reason for an allow_lock_order override (stored in the result's lock_order_override).

inputs.name: owner_id
inputs.description: v0.3 (R1b). The stable owner identity asserted on every op (defaults to holder). Part of the three-identity tuple owner_id + gpu_authority_epoch + resident_generation + exec_lease_id; check reports owner_current + authority_ok.

inputs.name: resident_generation
inputs.description: v0.3 (R1b). The PoolManager-owned per-launch generation, stamped into the lease and asserted on check (generation_current). res.lease carries + validates it; the PoolManager owns when it increments (server start/replace/invalidate).

inputs.name: transition
inputs.description: v0.3 (R1b) acquire. Engage the single scheduler-owned ATOMIC hand-off: reserve -> mint a new gpu_authority_epoch (fence the old owner) -> revoke a lower-priority pin -> drive the evictor OUTSIDE the lease mutex (drain/cancel/tree-kill/confirm-tree-gone/confirm-STABLE-headroom) under a crash-reconcilable txn journal -> grant ONLY if the reserved epoch is still current (else superseded_during_transition). Serialized: exactly one transition per resource at a time (equal priority does NOT preempt).

inputs.name: drain_timeout_ms
inputs.description: v0.3 (R1b) transition. Bounded drain of an ACTIVE exec before cancel -> supervisor tree-kill (in-flight revocation). Passed to the evictor seam.

inputs.name: headroom_observations
inputs.description: v0.3 (R1b) transition. WDDM discipline: headroom must be STABLE across this many observations (all >= required + target) before a grant.

inputs.name: headroom_stable_interval_ms
inputs.description: v0.3 (R1b) transition. Spacing between the stable-headroom observations.

inputs.name: reconcile
inputs.description: v0.3 (R1b). On check: roll a crashed IN-PROGRESS transition journal (PREPARING/DRAINING/STARTING) whose owner is stale or whose epoch was superseded to ABORTED (idempotent). A transition also auto-reconciles on entry.

inputs.name: authority_epoch
inputs.description: v0.3 (R1b). Assert-this-epoch: an alias of fencing_token for renew/release/check CAS (a superseded actor is FENCED OUT). Side effects ASSERT the epoch; they never advance it.

inputs.name: lease_dir
inputs.description: Override the shared lease directory (default $env:LIFEORCH_LEASE_DIR, else runtime/leases). All processes MUST resolve the same dir. The durable per-resource fencing counter (<resource>.fence) + transition journal (<resource>.txn) live here too.

outputs.description: acquire: {acquired, lease_id, holder, expires_at_utc, ttl_seconds, waited_ms, reclaimed_stale, already_held, held_by}; +v0.2 when engaged: {fencing_token, lease_kind, priority, revocable, revoked_by, revocation_signaled?, revoked_pin?, prepared?, required_vram_mib?, target_headroom_mib?, free_vram_mib?, evict_performed?, headroom_confirmed?, evictor_mode?, evictor_outcome?, lock_order_override?, reason?}; +v0.3 when engaged: {gpu_authority_epoch, exec_lease_id, resident_generation, owner_id}; +v0.3 transition: {transition, transition_id, transition_state (RESERVING|PREPARING|DRAINING|STARTING|COMMITTED|ABORTED), tree_gone, headroom_observations, superseded, reconciled?}. release: {released, reason, held_by} (+fence_stale on a stale -FencingToken/-AuthorityEpoch). renew: {renewed, lease_id, expires_at_utc, renew_count, reason} (+fencing_token/revoked_by; reason fence_stale|revoked). status: {exists, held, stale, holder, lease_id, expires_at_utc, seconds_remaining} (+v0.2 fields when engaged). check: {exists, held, stale, holder, lease_id, fencing_token, lease_kind, revocable, revoked_by, priority, expires_at_utc, seconds_remaining, token_current, fence_status} (+v0.3 when engaged: gpu_authority_epoch, exec_lease_id, resident_generation, owner_id, owner_current, generation_current, authority_ok, reconciled?). list: {count, leases:[...]}. A plain (no-v0.2/v0.3-input) acquire/release/renew/status/list is BYTE-IDENTICAL to v0.1.
